summary: Halyard template mutual NDA with Kranwerk's entity details, a named-product Purpose, carve-outs moved into the definition, GDPR and notice tweaks, and a margin query on equitable relief; substantive positions remain within the playbook.

findings.quote: KRANWERK INDUSTRIE AG
findings.why: Counterparty has inserted its entity name, German registration and Munich address, which the lawyer must confirm against the commercial register (RQ07).

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either Party can be either, and the obligations bind the Receiving Party whichever Party that is.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: concerning the evaluation of Halyard's enterprise resource allocation software
findings.why: The Purpose is still limited to discussions about a potential commercial relationship, now tied to a named product evaluation.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: (a) is in, or enters, the public domain other than as a direct or indirect result of a breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives;
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third party, independently developed) are retained with the same wording and written-records evidence standard, but moved from clause 3 into the definition.
findings.fallback_cited: Different wording or location (including inside the definition) with the same substance.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (including advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis with the recipient liable for them.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Disclosure is allowed where required by law, court, regulator or stock exchange, notice only where legally permitted, and resistance is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and exceptions for automated backups and legally required copies, which stay confidential.

findings.quote: in England [[INS: or the State of Bavaria, Germany,]] when banks in London [[INS: and Munich]] are open for business
findings.why: Business Day definition now also counts Bavarian holidays and Munich bank days, a customary mechanical change that lengthens deadlines slightly without altering any substantive position.
findings.fallback_cited: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: IP stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted other than use solely for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Mutual as-is and no-warranty wording, fraud carve-out kept, and no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: [[INS: the Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation),]]
findings.why: Adding EU GDPR to the definition is consistent with clause 9, which limits personal data to business contacts and requires a separate DPA before any other sharing.
findings.fallback_cited: Counterparty clause committing both parties to UK GDPR / EU GDPR compliance and a separate DPA before sharing personal data.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Three-year survival with Trade Secrets protected for as long as they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual 'entitled to seek' equitable relief with cumulative remedies in 11.2; the margin comment queries it as unfamiliar to German law but asks only for a procedural-rules wording, not a change to the substance (RQ04).

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner
findings.why: No assignment by either Party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: [[INS: (or international courier service in the case of international delivery)]]
findings.why: Notice clause now allows international courier with a five Business Day deemed receipt, which is customary boilerplate drafting.
findings.fallback_cited: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales, unchanged by the counterparty.
